title: The testing pyramid: cost, speed and confidence at each layer

videos.script: For twenty lessons this course has sold you the browser test. This one asks what it costs. {{one-behaviour}} You take one behaviour of the shop. A banana goes into the basket, and the total says five reais ninety. You check it three times, at three layers. {{three-layers}} A unit test calls the function that adds up the basket, with no server and no browser. An API test asks the server, with no browser. And a browser test clicks the button, the way a customer does. {{clock}} Then you time all three, once and twenty times, and draw the pyramid with your own numbers. {{defects}} Next you break the shop twice, on purpose. One break only the browser test sees. The other, only the unit test pins down, and the browser test stays green. So no layer is enough on its own. {{shapes}} You meet three shapes a suite can take: the pyramid, the ice-cream cone and the trophy. Each one is an argument about where to spend. {{top}} And you finish with a question to ask of every browser test you write. Could a cheaper layer see this? If it could, the test goes down. If it could not, it has earned its place.
